messages:
alex: quick handoff — running summary of the midday incident so the night crew has context. TL;DR: embeddings service (embed-io) saw a sustained p95 token-latency spike between ~11:08–11:32 UTC, some requests timed out, we triaged and applied a traffic-split fallback. impact: ~3% of global embedding requests retried, one enterprise customer (AcmeCorp) saw frontend 504s. full timeline below.

incident-bot: [ALERT] alerts/embeddings-high-p95 triggered (p95 token latency > 1200ms) — routed to #pager.

alex: what we did during the shift:
- primary (me) received the pager, confirmed increase in host-side queuing on node pool embed-pool-2.
- root cause hypothesis: delayed KV-cache fetches due to occasional redis worker stall; we saw many long tail latencies from redis reads.
- immediate mitigation: enabled model-level fallback in routing policy to send 15% of traffic to embed-compact variant which has smaller KV lookup footprint. That brought p95 down under alert threshold within ~6 minutes.

sam: added: verified canary logs showed reduced token timeouts after reroute. I pushed a temporary routing override: `route.set("embed-io", {fallback_ratio:0.15, reason:"midday-redis-stall"})` and added a short-lived alert to watch retries.

maria: noted customer impact — AcmeCorp had ~40 failed calls during the window; their SDK retried twice and surfaced 504s to their dashboard. I opened INC-2026-348 for customer outreach and tagging in the CRM.

jordan-ops: runbook pointers for the night: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/embeddings-kv-stalls (see section "fast fallback + traffic-split")
- if p95 recurs after reroute, escalate to eng-runtime and eng-ml (oncall pager).

lee: operational checks I ran:
- `kubectl top pods -n embed | grep embed-node` — no sustained CPU / mem saturation.
- `redis-cli --latency-history` returned spikes correlated to the incident window.
- verified autoscaler didn't throttle replica count during the event.

alex: coverage gaps / TODOs for incoming shift:
- primary/secondary for overnight EU coverage not swapped in rotation (we're missing an assigned EU secondary next week). @maria please coordinate with oncall-schedule to plug EU nights.
- follow-up action: reduce default routing fallback threshold from 15% to 10% after verification to limit cost.
- create perf-test to repro long-tail redis read latencies against embed-compact. ticket: ENG-OPT-1912.

maria: I'll take ownership of customer comms for AcmeCorp, will share a draft in #customer-success. Also will file the schedule change request (assigning Jordan as EU secondary for next two rotations).

sam: monitoring changes I applied:
- temporary alert `alerts/embeddings-client-retries` added (>= 1.5% retries in 5m).
- lowered alert aggregation window to 3m for the next 24h to catch reappearance.

alex: handoff checklist for next oncall (please ack):
- primary: alex (currently passing to night crew)
- secondary: jordan-ops
- known mitigations active: 15% traffic split to embed-compact (routing override id `ro-2026-8743`), retry-alert active, incident ticket INC-2026-348 created.
- runbooks: embeddings-kv-stalls, embedding-fallback-playbook (links posted above).
- customer-facing: AcmeCorp contact point assigned, CS ticket open.
- follow-ups: ENG-OPT-1912 perf test, review redis client timeouts across pools, schedule fix for EU night secondary.

lee: ack from me — I'll watch redis latency dashboards for the next 6h and keep the `redis-healer` playbook on standby.

jordan-ops: ack — I'll be secondary. If things worsen, I'll open an emergency bridge and escalate to eng-runtime.

alex: final notes: no data loss, degrade-to-fallback kept service available but increased token cost by ~4% during the window. If you need quick commands for rollback of the override:
```
# remove override
route.delete("ro-2026-8743")
# confirm rollout
route.get("embed-io").policy
```

alex: handing over to night crew — please ping me if any alert fires with matching signatures (p95 token latency > 1.2s + client retries > 2%). Thanks. :thumbsup:
